invariants: Applications own OpenTelemetry providers, exporters, flushing, and shutdown
Logs use the next-loggers/v1 envelope with trace and span correlation
Payloads, tokens, email addresses, entity identifiers, and other PII are never emitted
Metric dimensions and log attributes use bounded reviewed vocabularies
Telemetry failures are best effort and never change product correctness
Flutter mobile persists the visible row and durable outbox atomically in SQLite
Browser storage uses IndexedDB or SQLite Wasm with the same atomic outbox contract
Every mutation has a permanent mutation identifier and an observed base revision
Revisions and ordered cursors decide conflicts; timestamps never decide a winner
JSON and jsonb conflict checks use structural deep equality and three-way merge
Realtime notifications are wake hints and never replace a durable ordered pull cursor
Shared Auth verification and direct Supabase user verification race concurrently
The first verified identity may authenticate without waiting for the slower authority
One authority error does not cancel or invalidate a success from the other authority
Both authorities must be definitely invalid before returning unauthenticated
Timeouts, transport failures, and contradictory identities fail closed as degraded
Shared Auth roles are authoritative; a direct Supabase identity has no privileged roles
Service credentials are accepted only by explicitly machine-scoped endpoints
Every reusable package root declares .zpkg.toml and commits .zpkg.lock
CI validates the manifest and installs with frozen immutable lock state
Mutable Git references and unverified locally seeded registry entries are forbidden
Git submodule revisions and matching Zed source revisions cannot disagree
Unavailable dependencies remain explicitly pending instead of receiving fabricated locks
